prior_importants.description: The carried-importants line also counts importants that were anchored in an earlier round and still have a thread. Resolving that thread used to release the PR. Now the PR stays `review-open` until a later round finds the code changed, so a declined or dismissed important holds it indefinitely.

`.at(-1)` also selects a no-verdict round's summary ("**Not reviewed.** Nothing in this round is a verdict…"), which has no count lines. A failed round therefore cancels the importants still open from the last complete review. If the head then moves without a new review, the PR reads `ready`.

findings.description: unthreadedImportants subtracts one for every `- `path:N` (` line that follows any line shaped like a carried count header, with no limit and no dedupe. Finding text inside the summary body can contain such lines at column 0, so it can push the count of unthreaded importants to zero and release a PR to `ready` while an important it carried is still unthreaded. The workflow comment says finding text 'could only hold a PR in review'; that is no longer true.

The new tests run `unthreadedImportants` and `isVerdict` on their own, but nothing tests how the workflow wires them in. Two edits would pass every test and bring back the prior importants: removing the `Re:` → `path:line` mapping in `botThreads`, or dropping `isVerdict` from the summary filter. A reworded `Re:` prefix in `commentBody` would also go unnoticed.

A carried entry matches any bot thread at the same `path:line`, including a resolved thread left by a different, earlier finding. So an important that was carried unanchored at that exact line is subtracted, and the PR can read `ready` while it is still open.

isVerdict's comment says it matches "the body's first line only", but the code reads line index 2, the first line after `REVIEW_HEADING` and its blank line. A reader changing the renderer is not told that the match depends on that fixed offset.

process_issues.description: The correctness reviewer tagged its test-adequacy finding (pr-status-workflow.test.ts:99-134) important, but its own report says both fixes are correct as rendered today, so nothing breaks at this head. The orchestrator retagged it nit before consolidation (§6: the tag must match the body).

The validated security finding comes with a fix the validator confirmed only for the reported path. A real carried entry's multi-line description can still use up its own block's budget, so the fix is in the body as code and `suggestion` is null.
